correctness.rationale: The repaired claim retains the scalar stochastic theorem, corrects the source comparison (the source uses run-constant, horizon-dependent parameters, not an iteration-indexed diminishing schedule), and credits the already-known deterministic boundary. Reconstructed the affine scaled matrix and Schur conditions: its quadratic factor has q(1)=t and q(−1)=4−3t with constant term 1−t; the remaining eigenvalue is 1−α. At and above 4/3, exactly one simple real eigenvalue is ≤−1 and the others have modulus less than one. Independent noise contributes a sum of squared first-coordinate impulse coefficients; the stated controllability and observability determinants t and −α make the dominant coefficient nonzero, so the risk actually diverges, including at equality. For the variance, the normalized momentum variance is α/(2−α), and the two cross terms come from a linear system with determinant α²+(1−α²)t. Stationarity of λ/η, whose increment is t times the next primal iterate, gives C₁₂=tC₁₁/2. Combining that with the next primal variance yields the stated risk, with physical scale σ²/η². Independently checked the strict log second derivative by comparing 3/(4−3t) with (1−α)/(2−α−(1−α)t), and the signs at 2/3 and 1. The logarithmic derivative extends continuously in α on the closed bracket; its only zeros at the endpoint parameters are the stated limits. The optimizer holds at fixed η and α while varying β/η. The repaired auxiliary files correct garbled parameter notation, checker filename, and the description of covariance checks; the checker was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: This is the smallest equality-constrained model in which feasibility, a dual state and filtered gradient noise all interact. The exact stationary calculation answers how to choose the penalty against persistent oracle noise, including a strictly interior optimizer with different limits at slow refresh and near-unfiltered noise. It also separates a noiseless spectral threshold from actual divergence of forced feasibility variance. The value is in that tuning distinction and explicit risk, not in renaming the known 4/3 boundary or in extrapolating a scalar optimizer to general MALM.
